subject: language
intro: Ms. Kim here. Let's plan a lesson on evaluating whether an argument is sound.

beats.narration: Advertisements are a great, relatable entry point.
This standard asks students to evaluate an argument and whether its reasoning and evidence are sound.
"Relevant and sufficient" are the key words from the standard.
beats.text: Students will be able to evaluate an argument by determining whether its evidence is relevant and sufficient and identifying irrelevant evidence.

beats.narration: Students are experts at being skeptical of ads.
beats.text: Show two product ads. "Which one makes a stronger argument? Why?"

beats.narration: Finding irrelevant evidence is the hardest part, so I model it.
beats.text: Model evaluating an op-ed: identify the claim, list the evidence, and ask of each piece: Is it relevant? Is there enough? Point out one piece of irrelevant evidence.

beats.narration: Comparing two arguments makes the evaluation more meaningful.
beats.text: Groups evaluate two op-eds on the same topic using a rubric (relevant, sufficient, credible) and decide which is stronger.

beats.narration: This checks the most challenging skill.
beats.text: Identify one piece of evidence in today's op-ed that is weak or irrelevant, and explain why.

outro: Ads, model, compare, evaluate. Your turn.
